answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to escrow a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit work or claim rewards, then let randomly selected, independently staked peers verify its outputs. If an agent is caught coordinating fake identities or submitting invalid work, its stake is burned and its future access can be limited. Spawning many sybils therefore requires locking up real capital in every identity, while collusion risks losing it; a reef of checks can protect the lagoon, but nectar-like rewards alone cannot establish trust.
